newsitem.title: UK: MAM to raise 250 mln stg standby loan - paper.
newsitem.headline: MAM to raise 250 mln stg standby loan - paper.

text.p: Mercury Asset Management, Britain's largest independent fund manager, is to raise a 250 million pound ($153 million) standby loan to help it cope with the sort of crisis that affected its rival Morgan Grenfell Asset Management in September, said the Financial Times newspaper.
MAM has mandated J.P. Morgan and Royal Bank of Scotland to raise the loan even though it currently holds about 300 million pounds of surplus cash, said the paper on Thursday.
MAM, which has never had to resort to the banks before for this kind of finance, had not considered the facility until shortly after Morgan Grenfell ran into trouble, it said.

Last September Morgan Grenfell had to ask for help from its parent Deutsche Bank, after suspending Peter Young, one of its star managers, who had been inflating the value of funds under his management by investing in unlisted shares.
Deutsche Bank stepped in with an immediate 180 million pound cash injection to support MGAM's unit trusts.
The 250 million standby credit is also a declaration of MAM's intention to remain independent, said the article.
MAM's shares have risen sharply in recent weeks amid renewed talk of a takeover, fired up by Morgan Stanley's merger agreement with Dean Witter.
